clue.text: The way in which one goes around bushy fence

indicators.note: 'in which' says the next piece sits inside the phrase that comes before it

blocks.note: how something is done is the way it is done
an edger works its way around the border of a lawn

explanation.surface: A walker follows a path that winds around a shaggy roadside fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bushy fence' is the definition; 'one goes around' describes a gardener's tool for trimming lawn borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of shrubs planted along a field boundary, serving as a living barrier.

clue.text: Down-at-heel old solver given hiding!

indicators.note: something given a hiding place is tucked away inside the letters around it

blocks.note: surface padding: part of the phrase for shabby, giving no letters
the letters run across the end of 'at' and into 'heel'

explanation.surface: A shabby old puzzler gets a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' pretends to mean a beating. The solver is 'you', addressed by the clue, and THEE is the archaic form of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords address their solver as 'you', and the archaic object form of that pronoun is the old word here.

clue.text: Rising corrosion is added to woe

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: rust is corrosion of iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spreading rust only adds to someone's misery.
explanation.walkthrough: TSURIS is a Yiddish word, also spelt tsores, used in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsuris is Yiddish for trouble, misery and aggravation, so it matches sorrow or distress.

clue.text: Location of the Taj Mahal school, leading the way in gout ...

indicators.note: something leading the way goes in front, so this piece is placed first

blocks.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the Taj Mahal stands in the Indian city of Agra

explanation.surface: A school in Agra pioneers treatment of gout.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Podagra is the medical term for gout, especially when it attacks the big toe.

clue.text: ... in twist, Medical Unit grew quite animated

indicators.note: 'in' places the following unit inside the word for twist

blocks.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
MED is a standard short form of medical
U is short for unit

explanation.surface: A hospital department in turmoil became quite excited.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue only; the wordplay starts fresh here.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm up is to become livelier and more enthusiastic, as a party or a crowd does.

clue.text: Remarkable place, Londres, endlessly changing - stick around!

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the French city name is dropped
changing means the letters are rearranged into a new order
around means the stick wraps itself about the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a wand is a thin stick
the French name for London, without its last letter

explanation.surface: London, in its French form, is a wonderful place, but stay a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Londres is the French name for London; the stick splits into two parts either side of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonderland is any place full of marvels, after the magical world Alice discovers.

clue.text: With redundancy on the increase

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
axing staff is making them redundant

explanation.surface: Job losses are going up.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is said to be waxing when its lit part grows, so the word means growing larger.

clue.text: Devil of a translation from this poem!

indicators.note: a translation renders the material in new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem proves fiendishly hard to translate.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephisto, short for Mephistopheles, is the devil of the Faust legend, famously the subject of Goethe's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto is the demon to whom Faust sells his soul, so he is a devil by name.

clue.text: Market boiler with gold inlay

indicators.note: an inlay is set into a surface, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: an Aga is a British range cooker that also heats water
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A luxury stove with gold decoration goes on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron British range cooker; 'or' is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square of an ancient Greek city, used as a marketplace.

clue.text: He provokes fear so on his return

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A frightening man is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folklore, or any person who terrifies others.

clue.text: Completely bonkers to deliver club from Spain

blocks.note: real mad is slang for totally crazy
to deliver someone from harm is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: Somebody is completely crazy to hand over a Spanish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is the famous football team based in the Spanish capital.

clue.text: Corner pieces behind clubs in Staffs

indicators.note: behind means this piece follows the other one

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
rooks start in the corners of a chessboard

explanation.surface: Chess pieces trail behind the golf clubs in Staffordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffs looks like the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a shepherd's hooked stick, so crooks are a kind of walking staves.

clue.text: Starts taking steps - the problem for the 9-phobic

blocks.note: a show opens when it starts
paces are steps

explanation.surface: Someone starts walking, but steps are a problem for the nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is AGORA, so the 9-phobic is agoraphobic.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoraphobia is a fear of public places, literally of the marketplace, so wide expanses frighten sufferers.

clue.text: He's seen to get up in cowboy show

definitions.note: a character who appears on stage, in Othello

indicators.note: 'in' puts the outfit inside the show

blocks.note: a rodeo is a display of cowboy skills
a get-up or rig is an outfit

explanation.surface: A man is spotted standing up in a Wild West show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' reads as a verb but is the noun for a costume. The definition is cryptic: a character who is seen on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the foolish gull in Shakespeare's Othello, a figure audiences watch on stage.

clue.text: Tale in which feeble fellow replaces a con

indicators.note: replaces means one piece is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: taken as written
a weed is a weak, puny person
taken as written, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A story where a weakling takes the place of a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: WEED takes the place of the A in TALE: T(WEED)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweedle is an old verb meaning to cajole or wheedle someone, so to trick or swindle them.

clue.text: All in all, vocalic change needed in Wales

indicators.note: vocalic refers to vowels, so one vowel is swapped for another
a loose signal that the letters must be rearranged as required

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On balance, a change in vowel sounds is called for in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: One A of ALL IN ALL becomes E and the letters are rearranged; the definition is loose, a place in Wales. Llanelli is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in Carmarthenshire, south Wales, so it is found in that country.

clue.text: Fit trooper dropping into the Communist Machine

indicators.note: dropping into means one piece falls inside the other

blocks.note: fit as in suitable
a para is a parachute trooper

explanation.surface: A fit soldier parachutes into the Soviet party apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: A para is a member of a British parachute regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparat is the Russian term for the administrative organisation of the Communist Party.

clue.text: Seductive beau finally gets pulled in every call!

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
pulled in means drawn inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: every one is all
the last letter of beau
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A boyfriend is eventually reeled in by every phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like a summons, but it is the verb for phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring is attractive and tempting, drawing others towards it.

clue.text: Man in authority runs over deed to cause diversion

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means this piece sits above the next

blocks.note: the referee is in charge of a match
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: An official runs over some document, causing a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deed' suggests a legal document, but it means an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To refract is to bend a ray of light or sound as it passes into another medium, turning it aside.

clue.text: Waiting in the wings, having completed journey from Deadwood?

blocks.note: first meaning: out of the audience's view, ready to go on
second meaning: got down from a stagecoach at the end of the ride

explanation.walkthrough: The Deadwood Stage is the stagecoach in the song from the film Calamity Jane; a passenger at journey's end is off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor not yet on is behind the scenes, and a traveller who has alighted has got down from the coach.

clue.text: About to join in celebration - and that's as open as I can be

definitions.text: as open as I can be

indicators.note: to join in is to enter the event, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a fest is a festival or celebration
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to join a party and feels as candid as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' is a piece on its own and 'to join in' tells where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Freest is the superlative of free, meaning most unrestricted or unreserved.

clue.text: Cut society off

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
food that is off has gone bad, as an addled egg has

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut ... off' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Cut' is a noun: the butcher's cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle of lamb or venison is a joint of meat from the back, so it is a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Philosopher almost sent one up

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end
in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: sent without its last letter
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A philosopher very nearly dispatched a colleague upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman Stoic thinker and writer, tutor to the emperor Nero.

clue.text: A solid block of cheddar one's grated

indicators.note: grating cheese breaks it up, so these letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slab of hard cheese has been grated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A solid block' looks like the cheese, but 'A solid' alone is the definition, in its geometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A decahedron is a three-dimensional figure with ten faces, one kind of geometric solid.

clue.text: Fate: Hobson's choice of number

blocks.note: N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
a choice is this or that, and Hobson's offers no real alternative
the same number again, since Hobson's choice is no choice

explanation.surface: Fate leaves someone no real choice about which number to take.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson's choice means take what is offered or nothing, so the choice of number is N or N. The Norns are the three Fates of Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology a Norn is one of the female beings who spin the destinies of gods and people.

clue.text: Standard: Christie's choice in book

blocks.note: the title of an Agatha Christie spy novel featuring Tommy and Tuppence, posed as a choice of two letters

explanation.surface: A standard set by the choice of a novel by Agatha Christie.
explanation.walkthrough: Christie's novel N or M? offers a choice between two letters, which together spell NORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is an accepted standard or usual pattern against which things are measured.

clue.text: When seasick, does one feel this? Yes and no!

definitions.text: When seasick, does one feel this?

blocks.clueFragment: When seasick, does one feel this?
blocks.note: surface reading: asks whether you feel great when queasy on a boat
setter's reading: no, you do not feel great, but yes, you feel the heaving of the sea that caused it

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both 'excellent', as in feeling great, and the rolling movement of the sea; the seasick traveller feels one and not the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is both an old-fashioned word for splendid and the long rise and fall of ocean waves.

clue.text: Guides topping fellow into firm (Ulster)

indicators.note: into means the fellow is placed inside the word for firm

blocks.note: Co. is short for company
an icer puts the topping on cakes
Ulster is used to mean Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A splendid chap joins a Northern Irish company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like the old British word for excellent, but it means the icing on a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciceroni is the plural of cicerone, a guide who shows sightseers around museums and antiquities.
